lines:
Responsibilities: Maps normalized semantic items to messages and typed cards for plans, tool/MCP/external-agent activity, artifacts, approvals, routes, errors, verification, and repairs. Sanitizes rich text/links and labels reasoning_raw, reasoning_summary, progress, and assistant_output exactly as supplied.
Owned state: card expansion, selected card tab, copy feedback, renderer registry, and virtual-row measurements; payload/status remain immutable projections.
Contracts: accepts TimelineItemViewModel batches and RenderPolicy; emits typed retry/approval/artifact/fork/continue intents to Chat Workspace, EvidenceSelection to the inspector, and repair_candidate selection to Repair Review. UnknownTimelineItem preserves kind, source, timestamp, and safely escaped JSON.
Normative activity presentation contract: The normal conversation is a chronological activity feed; ParentSpanId supplies attribution and inspection context. Agent-loop and agent/model-call workflow-node containers do not occupy standalone input/output cards ahead of their children. Their normalized input/output and hierarchy remain available in Run details. A containing workflow node's failure or cancellation is a compact selectable status entry at its committed terminal sequence, rather than being displayed at the parent's start; an equivalent nested agent-loop status is suppressed. Model/tool invocation cards keep their stable span IDs and first committed sequence. Independent workflow steps and external-agent ownership remain visible. Siblings and every visible transition remain in committed order. If execution is ModelCall 1 -> causally linked ToolCall -> ModelCall 2, the UI shows exactly that; it must not put the tool beneath still-running reasoning or merge later reasoning into the earlier call. Every activity can expose actual normalized redacted Input from SpanStarted and Output/Error from its terminal event, using artifact links when large; tool cards show called tool/arguments and returned result/error. Running/waiting/terminal status derives only from committed lifecycle events. Workflow Input, Output, and Wait plumbing spans remain inspectable but are hidden from normal Chat when redundant. Primary assistant_output renders once as the chat answer; an Output-node card cannot repeat it. Equal or semantically redundant input/output sections are omitted. RenderPolicy changes visibility only, never history or order.

Failure/degraded behavior: missing renderers never drop history; malformed rich content is escaped; missing artifacts and opaque sources are explicit; large payloads link to paginated evidence.
Performance/accessibility: virtualizes long histories, coalesces progress display without changing semantic order, uses navigable headings/status/action groups, rate-limited live regions, 200% zoom, and WCAG 2.2 AA.
Non-responsibilities: no provider-protocol interpretation, hidden-reasoning reconstruction, direct IPC, authorization, history persistence, or artifact execution.

Filesystem approvals: Present core-projected access and containing directory. One read permission covers listing, reading, search, grep and images; read/write adds editing and creation. Users choose directory/subtree or all external locations, then Allow for this chat or Always approve in project. Approve once remains invocation-only; denial carries a reason. Renderer sends typed selections only; the core validates owner, canonical scope and access before committing.

Native subagent attribution (2026-09-19; background children 2026-09-21): A model/tool span beneath a tool_call with capabilityId=tool.subagent belongs to the subagent actor, as do descendants of an external_agent span and every span whose committed parentSpanId ancestry reaches a delegated-child evidence root. Attribute native child reasoning and speech through committed parentSpanId ancestry in both live projection and replay; keep the owning workflow node for inspection without presenting child speech as the main Agent's. An inline child shares the delegating pass's span tree. A background child outlives the delegating pass, so it commits to an independent evidence root in the same Run history whose root span carries subagentChildId and is attributed to the subagent actor; the parent's tool span records the child id and the durable ChildContextFrameV1 keeps the lineage. A parent span is never kept open merely to hold a background child.

Subagent tab scope (2026-09-21): The same presenters render a delegated child's activity when the Chat Workspace selects a subagent tab. The renderer accepts a child scope and shows only activities belonging to that child's evidence root, leaving the parent Chat unaffected. A read-only child header shows the child's task, status and lineage back to the parent. The child view never offers composer input, steering or approval, and never synthesizes unknown or not-yet-loaded child activity. The tool block for tool.subagent and tool.subagent_fork exposes an open action that activates the child's tab, keyed by the card's committed childId.

Question and path dialogs (2026-09-21): A committed question renders twice from one projection: a selectable `question` timeline card that keeps the durable prompt, its options, the chosen answer and the terminal outcome visible in chronology, and a modal dialog that is the focused answering surface. The dialog is a real modal (role=dialog, aria-modal, labelled heading, focus trap, Escape only after nested controls decline it, focus restored to the invoking surface) that opens when an unanswered question arrives and can be dismissed without answering, leaving the card answerable later; it never renders a stale question, never reopens a question that is already answered or cancelled, and never blocks Run details inspection. Controls are radio-group options in committed order, an optional free-text field when the tool allowed one, a default marked as such, Submit, and Skip/cancel, with keyboard order and rate-limited live status following the existing card rules. A tool.browse question renders the same dialog with its prompt, the currently chosen path and one button that opens the operating system's own file or folder chooser; the chosen path is sent to the core only when the user confirms, and dismissing the OS chooser leaves the dialog unchanged. A cancelled question is shown as cancelled, and the model receives that cancellation as its tool result.

Conversation path actions (2026-09-22): A path the conversation shows is never activated by a plain left click; a right-click on an element that already carries a path opens a small menu. The targets are an explicit markdown link whose target is a workspace-relative or absolute path, and the workspace path rendered on a read, write, edit, list, search or grep tool card, which now names the file its call acted on instead of repeating the tool identifier. The menu offers Open in default application, Open in editor and Reveal in folder, and it asks the trusted core to resolve the path first, so it can name the resolved absolute location before anything happens and can disable every entry with the core's own reason when the path is missing or lies outside the Chat's frozen workspace. Only the explicit menu choice performs an action, and a refused or failed action is reported through the existing notification publisher with the path and the reason. Bare paths inside prose are not linkified, and in a browser preview or without a Chat to resolve against the targets stay inert.
